object_description: inverted-T volume with two connected cruciform accommodation buildings
design_condition: The project is set parallel to the Allée des Marais as a single strong mass on the plain, contrasting with the organic neighbouring complex and leaving weakly connected exterior spaces around the enclosure.

positive.statement: The strength of the composition produces a clear simplicity of reading.
The facade treatment differentiates functions through window sizes while maintaining a common architectural principle.
The work on the cell's window size, proportion, and position demonstrates mastery of the subject.
The logistical circulations are concentrated and secure, providing a good economy of means.
The service courtyards efficiently serve all the workshops from the entrance area.
The phasing is well thought out.

negative.statement: The symmetrical composition raises questions about identification and does not optimally support the resocialization objective.
Many ground-level facades are blind, depriving prisoners of direct exterior views.
The limited material palette creates a cold atmosphere that does not correspond to ordinary living conditions.
The insertion into the landscape is not completely convincing, and the exterior spaces are weakly treated.
The concave wings limit clear views from the cells.
The wings stop somewhat arbitrarily without a convincing treatment of their ends.
The monolithic nature of the project makes phasing more complex and raises questions about its presence in the landscape and users' appropriation.
